fact: The regulator INCM reported in a communique of 21 August 2026 that a new licensing regulation, adopted by decree in July 2026, lets it convert operators' fines into universal-service obligations to fund actions improving access in universal-service areas.

INCM, through the Universal Access Service Fund (FSAU), announced 60 new mobile stations with public Wi-Fi centres in rural areas of nine provinces under the government's Rural Connectivity Project, awarded to Vodacom Mozambique by tender INCM/CP/117/2025 (doubled from 30).

INCM, with the Universal Access Service Fund (FSAU), opened a public tender for the first phase of its Rural Connectivity Project, covering at least 30 pre-selected rural locations with 2G/4G infrastructure and public Wi-Fi multimedia centres; bids were due 19 September 2025.

The Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation announced on 17 August 2026 a target of extending telecom services to at least 300 localities, with the Rural Connectivity Project run through the FSAU with operators.
The government says it has already connected 149 localities to the internet and 418 schools.

The statement says the Universal Access Service Fund (FSAU) is an initiative to provide broadband internet in rural areas, especially district headquarters, through projects including Rural Connectivity and Internet in Schools; no sites counted.

The regulator INCM said on 17 October 2025 it would deploy 60 new mobile base stations in nine provinces under the Universal Access Service Fund with Vodacom Mozambique, to bring mobile and internet service to communities without coverage; no site is yet reported connected.

fact: The government, through regulator INCM, and operators launched a rural connectivity pilot under 'Internet for All by 2030' on 28 April 2025 in Xinavane; two satellite-backed antennas are installed, in Xinavane and Pessene, each able to reach around 15,000 people.
